latest.text:
Shelton beat Fils in three sets at the ATP Finals and it was his first ever win at this event.

He played a very strong first set. Fils got out of an early game on his serve but Shelton broke him twice after that and won 5 games in a row to take it 6–2, mixing big serves into the body with wide ones. Fils pushed hard in the second set and won some of the best points of the match. He broke late, then had to save break points while he served for the set but he held to take it 6–3 and make it one set all.

The deciding set turned early. Shelton broke for 2–0, though it took him several chances in that game and then had to protect that lead. Fils had two chances to break back before Shelton held for 4–1 and Fils got one more look when Shelton served for the match. Shelton held again and won the set 6–3. Credit to him: once he was ahead in the third, he never gave the break back.

68% behind his second serve shows why Fils found it so hard to break him, far above his 53% average on hard. His backhand was a real weapon too, with several clean winners.

Shelton did what he had to do but it was not perfect: he made 32 unforced errors and that is what he has to clean up for the next match. He plays Jodar next.

latest.text:
Zverev beat Jodar in straight sets in the opening singles match of the week in Turin, against a 20-year-old who was playing the event for the first time.

It was not easy for either of them. The ball was not flying through the air on this fast indoor court and both players seemed to struggle at times to control it. Jodar held well early on but Zverev broke him late in the first set and served for it. Jodar had two break points in that game, the only chances he got all match and Zverev saved both to take the set 6–4. The second set followed the same pattern. Zverev broke early, did not see another break point and took it 6–4 as well.

That serve was the whole story, because Jodar barely got a look at it. Zverev won 86% of the points behind his first serve, against his 74% average on hard. He was also the more clutch of the two on the big points.

It was not perfect but it did not need to be. It was not his best return performance and he let most of his break points go. Still, one break in each set was enough and the moment that decided it came when he held while serving for the first set. Shelton waits in his next match.

commentary.text: Zverev beat Jodar 6-4, 6-4 in just under an hour and a half, in the opening singles match of the week. Jodar, aged 20 and making his debut at the event, came through his first two service games well but his serve was named as an area where he can still improve. The ball was not flying through the air and the players seemed to struggle at times to control it. Zverev served big and posted a high first serve percentage, taking the first set after 40 minutes. The second set followed a similar pattern. Jodar's movement and athleticism were good enough to compete at this level but Zverev's serving proved a little too much for him.
